finding.claim: Duration ISO string parsing slices from group 2 onward and never applies the leading -/+ sign captured in group 1, so negative durations parse as positive.

repro.testCode:
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import dayjs from './index.js'
import duration from './plugin/duration/index.js'

dayjs.extend(duration)

const start = dayjs('2023-01-01')
const twoWeeksObj = dayjs.duration({ weeks: 2 })
const twoWeeksIso = dayjs.duration('P2W')

assert.equal(twoWeeksObj.weeks(), 2)
assert.equal(twoWeeksIso.weeks(), 2)
assert.equal(start.add(twoWeeksObj).format('YYYY-MM-DD'), '2023-01-15')
assert.equal(start.add(twoWeeksIso).format('YYYY-MM-DD'), '2023-01-15')
assert.equal(dayjs('2023-01-15').subtract(dayjs.duration({ weeks: 1 })).format('YYYY-MM-DD'), '2023-01-08')
assert.equal(dayjs('2023-01-15').subtract(dayjs.duration('P1W')).format('YYYY-MM-DD'), '2023-01-08')
assert.equal(start.add(dayjs.duration({ weeks: 1, days: 1 })).format('YYYY-MM-DD'), '2023-01-09')
repro.expectedBehavior: Adding a Duration with a weeks component to a Dayjs date advances the date by 7 days per week (and subtracting moves it back), e.g. 2023-01-01 + P2W = 2023-01-15.
repro.rationale: manipulateDuration in plugin/duration/index.js adds years/months/days/hours/minutes/seconds/ms but never weeks, so a Duration parsed from {weeks} or 'P2W' (where days() is 0 and weeks() is stored separately) is dropped when added to a date.
repro.reason: the repository's own imports are not directly executable by Node without a build step (extensionless specifiers)
